#5446. 8 best Florida real estate schools for 2026

Our editors independently review the products we recommend. When you buy through our links, we may earn a commission. Learn more

Are you ready to begin a fulfilling real estate career in the Sunshine State? To get started, you have to complete 63 hours of prelicensing coursework through a state-approved real estate school before you’re allowed to take the licensing exam. Most schools offer this online now, which makes it easier to work through the material without putting your life on hold.

Not all online Florida real estate schools are the same. Some are better if you want structure and support while others work well if you just want to get through the coursework at your own pace. We’ve broken down the best online Florida real estate schools for 2026, comparing course formats, pricing, study tools and exam prep so you can choose the option that actually fits how you learn and fits your budget.

The CE Shop earns our top spot for one simple reason – it combines strong course content with tools that actually help students pass the exam. Features like a five-day free trial, a pass guarantee and its Exam Prep Edge study tools are all included with higher-tier packages, making it easier to prepare without having to guess what you’ll need to pass the exam.

Their platform is easy to use and includes short, self-paced lessons that allow you to fit lessons into your busy schedule without losing your place. Exam Prep Edge includes quizzes, flashcards, matching exercises and practice tests that reinforce key concepts as you go. For students thinking beyond licensing, the Premium Package also includes first-time renewal coursework and access to the Kickstarter Professional Development Program, which covers business planning, lead generation and negotiation basics.

The CE Shop offers four prelicensing course packages, plus Florida real estate continuing education and broker licensing courses in Florida. All three top-tier prelicensing packages include Exam Prep Edge to help you retain information and ace the exam.

Aceable Agent takes an innovative approach to online learning, with classes offered through its website, unique mobile app and podcast-style audio courses. Its self-paced and cost-effective Florida real estate courses help you learn on the go, so your study schedule can fit your busy life. Courses include engaging videos, interactive games, infographics and knowledge checks that use straightforward language and real-life scenarios inside bite-sized lessons to keep you engaged with the material.

Designed by learning science experts using proven instructional principles, Aceable Agent’s easy-to-understand courses have frequent practice tests, so you’ll go into the state exam feeling confident. Mastery Tracking helps you focus your energy on your weakest areas when studying for your course final and state licensing exams.

Aceable Agent offers three self-paced prelicensing course packages that include audio and video lessons and practice questions. Their Deluxe and Premium packages incorporate additional features like instructor support, exam prep, AI tools and live webinars.

Colibri Real Estate is a great option for students who want structure and help staying on track to meet their learning goals. With hundreds of thousands of agents trained by Colibri, their focus is on providing structured coursework with support from local real estate experts. The online platform is built around accountability by tracking your study time, setting weekly goals and clearly showing your progress, which can be helpful if you do better with defined milestones.

Colibri offers courses with interactive lessons and practice exams designed to reinforce key concepts as you move through the material. The courses also offer exam prep options, even in the lower-priced packages. The standard package includes practice tests and live Q&A sessions. Higher-tier packages include CompuCram Exam Prep with flashcards, audio reviews, readiness assessments and simulated exams. The Ultimate Learning package includes career resources such as how-to videos, checklists and a customizable business plan.

Colibri Real Estate offers four Florida prelicensing course packages, along with options for continuing education and broker licensing. Higher-tier packages include additional exam prep tools and study resources.

Casa Academy is an innovative real estate school in Florida that focuses on audio and AI to make learning easy. While they do offer self-paced courses from your laptop, Casa also has all of their course available on Spotify so you can learn on the go. Each class is structured as an informative discussion, so you’ll get real-world knowledge from experts that you will apply to your future career.

In addition, the integrated AI, built with ChatGPT, is there to enhance your educational experience. The AI tutor remembers your weaknesses and helps you review them until they become strengths. It will prompt you with explanations, quick reviews and drills to keep your knowledge sharp so you’re ready to pass the real estate exam.

Casa Academy provides basic packages with all the course hours you need:

Kaplan Real Estate Education has several packages to help students get ready for the Florida licensing exam. The courses are structured and detailed, with clear explanations that make it easier to understand some of the tougher concepts that Florida requires to pass the exam. Students like having different ways to study, whether that’s watching an instructor online, working through printed materials or using practice tests to see where they stand.

Kaplan’s exam prep tools and student support are what set this school apart. The study guide is detailed, and the practice questions are worded the same way you’ll see them on the exam. If you want a course that keeps you focused and gives you plenty of practice before exam day, Kaplan should be at the top of your list. Even though it comes with a higher price tag, the detailed content is well worth the investment.

Gold Coast Schools is a good option for students who want live instruction and a more hands-on learning experience. While its online courses are powered by Colibri’s learning platform, Gold Coast operates as its own Florida-based school with a strong focus on instructor access and student support.

Although the school doesn’t offer a mobile app, it does stand out for its personalized guidance. Students can speak directly with career counselors when deciding which course to take. Gold Coast also offers classroom, livestream and online options, with courses available in both English and Spanish.

In addition to prelicensing, Gold Coast offers post-licensing, continuing education and broker licensing education. Prelicensing education is offered in three different packages outlined below.

RealEstateU offers a straightforward, courses-only package that saves you money. If you feel confident taking exams and preparing for them, this low-cost real estate course may be right for you. If not, RealEstateU also offers two premium course bundles that go beyond just passing the real estate exam. They provide real-world strategies for success in your new career, like negotiation strategies, how to convert leads and how to choose the right brokerage. You’ll also learn the business of practicing real estate, including expenses, earning potential, commission structures and more.

RealEstateU’s exam study guide is included in their two top-tier packages. It offers practice questions and four practice exams to test your knowledge. If you prefer, audio lessons are available or you can download lessons and study materials to access them offline – providing flexibility if you can’t access wifi or the internet.

RealEstateU’s Florida prelicensing course starts at $99, making it the most affordable option on our list. Exam prep and additional study resources may cost extra, so make sure you factor that into your total budget if you need extra support.

VanEd stands out for how clear it is about what students are signing up for. You get a five-day free trial with full course access, which makes it easier to decide if the format works for you before committing. VanEd has been developing real estate courses for more than 17 years, with content built by instructors who understand both the licensing process and what Florida students need to know to pass the exam.

The courses use a mix of videos, infographics, flashcards and interactive exercises to keep the material moving. VanEd also includes virtual field trips that connect concepts to real-world scenarios, which can help with retaining what you learn. Everything works across all devices, so you can study from your laptop, tablet or phone and pick up where you left off.

VanEd offers three course packages at an affordable price. The five-day free trial is included in every package.

To determine the very best Florida real estate schools, we conducted extensive research, rating each school based on the following:

Finally, we considered the schools with unique features and professional development opportunities that can have significant value for real estate agents. We do the research so you don’t have to, bringing it all together in this guide to the best real estate schools in Florida. All that’s left for you to do is choose one and launch your new career.

The cost to get your real estate license in Florida depends mostly on the school and course package you choose. The biggest expense is the required 63-hour prelicensing course, which can range from lower-cost, self-paced options to more expensive packages that include exam prep, instructor access, or career resources. On top of that, Florida charges separate fees for the license application and the state exam.

When you add everything up, most people can expect to spend somewhere between $180 and $600 to get licensed. If you stick with a basic course, you’ll be closer to the lower end – and vice versa.

How long it takes to become a Florida real estate agent depends on how quickly you complete the required steps. The state requires 63 hours of prelicensing coursework, which some people finish in a few weeks if they move quickly, while others take a couple of months studying part-time. Once you complete the course, you’ll need to pass the state exam and submit your license application.

For most people, the process can take anywhere from one to three months. It depends on whether you’re studying full-time or part-time and what other commitments you may be juggling at the same time.

Once you have passed the real estate licensing exam, you can apply for a Florida real estate sales associate license online. In fact, Florida prioritizes flexibility, allowing licensees to take the prelicensing course, submit their license application and even take the state exam online through Pearson VUE proctoring.

The Florida Real Estate License Exam tends to be one of the more difficult to pass. There are 100 multiple-choice questions on the Florida real estate licensing exam, and the required passing score is 75%. According to the data available on Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation (DBPR), as well as other reputable digital resources and news sites, there is a 40-50% pass rate for those taking the Florida real estate exam for the first time. This makes it all the more important to make sure you choose the best real estate school to help you pass the exam on the first try.

According to Indeed, the average Florida real estate agent earns $101,676 annually (as of this writing), which is actually the same as the national average.

Getting your real estate license in Florida starts with choosing the right school helping you feel prepared on exam day and beyond. Some people need structure and guidance. Others just want a straightforward way to finish the coursework and move on. The schools in this guide give you options either way.

Our goal is to make the comparison easier by laying out what each school actually offers, so you can choose a course that fits your schedule, budget and learning style. As you move forward, you’ll find more how-to articles, real estate marketing tips, lead generation strategies and career resources at Vetted by HousingWire to help you keep building momentum beyond licensing.

#5444. Why biodiversity belongs in the master plan

Biodiversity can improve how parks, drainage and open space perform in master-planned communities. Studies cited show native plantings can lift pollinator abundance two to three times, and monitoring at Baseline recorded a 500% increase in macropollinators.   AI Summary

Master-planned communities have always been exercises in long-term thinking. Decisions about infrastructure, open space, water, landscaping and mobility made early in the planning process shape how a community functions decades later.

Parks, drainage areas and open spaces require substantial investment. But there’s growing evidence that designing those landscapes to support biodiversity can help that investment do more. Planned early as part of the infrastructure conversation, biodiversity can help a community better manage water, withstand environmental stress and create stronger connections between residents and the natural environment.

Pollinator habitats offer one of the most practical places to begin. Bees, butterflies and other pollinators help many flowering plants reproduce, sustaining vegetation that supports broader ecosystems.

Development decisions can remove or fragment the food sources and nesting areas those species need. At the scale of a master-planned community, developers have an opportunity to connect habitat across parks, drainage corridors and neighborhoods, making conservation part of the places people use every day.

Developers already expect infrastructure to serve a defined purpose and perform over time. Landscape systems deserve the same scrutiny.

A stormwater basin can manage runoff while also providing habitat. A trail corridor can connect residents to destinations while connecting pollinators to food and nesting resources. Plant selection can account for seasonal habitat needs alongside appearance and maintenance.

These decisions are much more than aesthetic considerations. A 2024 npj Urban Sustainability review examining research across stormwater management, water purification, heat mitigation, infrastructure resilience and maintenance costs found that biodiversity can meaningfully influence how blue-green infrastructure performs. More diverse ecological systems were associated with benefits ranging from improved stormwater retention and water purification to greater resilience under changing environmental conditions.

For developers, the implication is practical: Ecological and engineering performance do not necessarily need to be treated as separate objectives. Incorporating habitat into drainage or open-space plans creates opportunities to serve multiple purposes within the same land area. It also brings stewardship into the budget early, when responsibilities can be assigned, and maintenance requirements can inform design.

The value of parks, trails and public spaces extends beyond a direct line-item return. Planning those landscapes to support biodiversity adds another dimension to that investment, allowing them to contribute to ecological health while serving the needs of the community.

Pollinators depend on more than a patch of flowers. They need plants that provide resources throughout the growing season, places to nest and landscapes they can move through. An isolated garden may offer some of those resources, but a coordinated network can support them across a larger area.

Research shows how much landscape design can matter. A 2026 study published in Urban Ecosystems compared two newly developed residential neighborhoods and found that pollinator abundance and diversity were two to three times higher in the neighborhood dominated by native plants than in one with conventional landscaping. Despite similar numbers of flowers, the difference suggests that what developers plant can matter as much as how much they plant.

Master-planned communities have an unusual ability to create that network. Developers overseeing hundreds or thousands of acres can coordinate planting and habitat connections across property lines and development phases.

Rather than treating pollinator-friendly landscaping as a one-time intervention, the strategy needs to evolve alongside the community. Establishing baseline ecological conditions before construction and continuing monitoring as development progresses creates a reference point to evaluate changes over time.

That approach also requires considering habitat connectivity throughout the development process. Native plantings, open spaces and landscape corridors can be incorporated into the broader plan, rather than treated as isolated conservation features.

As developers, we routinely track home sales, water use, construction costs and other indicators of a community’s performance. Tracking ecological outcomes brings that same discipline to landscape investments.

At Baseline, a 1,100-acre master-planned community in Broomfield, Colorado, Butterfly Pavilion introduced its Pollinator District model in 2019, integrating conservation into development and ongoing operations. With monitoring in place before construction, researchers recorded 3,805 macropollinators in developed areas in 2025, up from 587 in 2023, an increase of more than 500%.

But numbers alone don’t tell the full story. Much of the increase came from nonnative western honeybees, making pollinator diversity an equally important measure of progress. The findings also highlight opportunities for additional native plantings to better support native bees.

The broader lesson is that ecological performance can be measured, and those findings can inform future decisions. Pollinator counts alone cannot establish the impact of every landscape intervention, but monitoring provides a way to identify changes, evaluate habitat strategies and adjust as development progresses.

That same principle can apply beyond pollinators. Whether evaluating stormwater systems, native landscaping or habitat corridors, establishing meaningful measures of performance can help developers better understand the long-term outcomes of their investments.

Integrating biodiversity also creates an ongoing opportunity to learn. Working with ecological specialists helps developers understand the starting landscape, set meaningful goals and see how it responds. That work needs to carry into everyday landscape care, from what gets planted to how areas are mowed and pests are managed, with resources and responsibility for stewardship established for the years ahead.

Monitoring can guide future plant selections and help identify gaps in habitat connections as new neighborhoods take shape. It also requires consistency and an understanding that ecological conditions vary with weather, seasonal timing and other factors.

Protected lands and conservation areas remain essential to ecological health, but developed communities can contribute, too. Places designed for people can also provide meaningful habitat when ecological considerations are incorporated into planning and long-term operations.

For developers, this is part of the longer commitment that comes with creating a master-planned community. These are places people will call home for decades, and caring for their ecological health is another part of planning for how they perform and evolve over that same horizon.

Kyle Harris is the Senior Vice President of Master Planned Communities at Realberry This column does not necessarily reflect the opinion of HousingWire’s editorial department and its owners. To contact the editor responsible for this piece: [email protected].

#5442. Chase launches Cyber Monday rate sale for purchase, refi loans

Chase Home Lending is offering a limited-time mortgage rate discount of up to 0.25% for eligible purchase and refinance loans. Borrowers must lock a rate from Nov. 30 through Dec. 13, and discounts can pair with select programs.  AI Summary

Chase Home Lending is offering a limited-time mortgage rate discount for eligible home purchase and refinance loans as borrowers continue to search for affordability.

The promotion runs from Nov. 30 through Dec. 13. Qualified borrowers could receive a rate discount of up to 0.25%, depending on their location and loan type.

Existing and new Chase customers must qualify for a purchase or refinance loan and lock in their rate during the promotional period. The company said there are no additional criteria to qualify for the sale.

“As millions of holiday shoppers look for the best online deals, the biggest purchase most people will ever make deserves the same kind of careful shopping,” Erik Schmitt, head of consumer direct sales at Chase Home Lending, said in a statement.

The rate discount can be combined with other available Chase Home Lending programs and discounts, subject to their terms and eligibility requirements. These include the Chase Homebuyer Grant and the bank’s Relationship Pricing Program, which recently expanded eligibility to more than 7 million small-business customers.

Maximum discounts and other limitations may apply depending on how the rate sale is combined with other programs, the company clarified.

November’s rate sale is not Chase’s first promotion this year.

In September, the lender offered qualified borrowers up to 0.25 percentage points off mortgage rates on purchase and refinance loans. The company also ran promotions in May, covering purchase and refinance loans, and in March, when it offered discounted rates on new purchase and refi loans.

In August 2025, Chase offered temporary discounts on purchase mortgages.

#5440. Report sheds light on China ties of some US-based Nvidia partners

An investigation has shed light on links between some Nvidia Corp. partners and companies that are based in China or are accused of breaching export controls.

The analysis was carried out by C4ADS, a Washington, D.C.-based nonprofit, at the request of CBS News. The outlet published the findings Wednesday evening.

The first focus of the investigation was a San Jose, California-based company called RiCloud AI Inc. It’s an Nvidia preferred partner, which means that it can buy the chipmaker’s high-end graphics processing units. Companies with that partner destination also have access to Nvidia’s GPU software and technical support services.

The investigation determined that RiCloud AI is a unit of Shenzen-based Yuxing InfoTech Investment Holdings Ltd. The latter company’s chief executive reportedly has a degree from a university run by China’s military. Yuxing’s chair, in turn, previously worked at a Chinese tech firm that drew national security scrutiny in Australia.

RiCloud AI recently signed a $120 million deal to lease Nvidia-powered servers to a Taiwanese whiskey company. The latter firm generated just $609,000 in profits last year.

The investigation also looked into a company called Topmost Corp. It’s reportedly linked to a California businessman who was recently indicted for allegedly smuggling GPUs to China.

According to CBS News, Topmost’s website states that it’s an authorized reseller of Nvidia partner 2CRSi Inc. The latter company makes servers powered by the chipmaker’s GPUs. Last month, it disclosed that it received a grand jury subpoena in connection with a client “we ourselves had reported to the authorities.”

The report also noted that California-based Aivres Inc. has exported $3 billion worth of Nvidia-powered servers to Southeast Asia since 2024. It’s a subsidiary of Inspur, a Chinese tech firm that is on the U.S. Commerce Department’s Entity List. Organizations on the list are subject to trade restrictions.

U.S. regulations prohibit companies from exporting Nvidia’s most advanced GPUs to China. Earlier this month, the Commerce Department closed a loophole that Chinese tech firms used to bypass those restrictions. The tech firms in questions rented access to Nvidia GPUs deployed in data centers outside China.

Some of the data centers used by Chinese companies are in Southeast Asia. On Wednesday, the Financial Times reported that Nvidia had instructed manufacturing partners to stop shipping GPU-equipped servers to four countries in the region. It’s reportedly unclear whether the move is temporary.

Separately, CNBC reported that companies have put an “unusually high” number of Nvidia GPUs up for sale since the Commerce Department announced the new restrictions. It’s believed the chips were intended for data centers that are used by Chinese firms. According to the report, thousands of high-end B300 GPUs are among the processors that were put up for sale.

You're viewing the US website. Looking for the Site edition?

From Aura digital picture frames to the Pocket AI voice recorder, here are great office gadgets that are discounted for Black Friday.

As the workday progresses, you face small problems. Your phone is almost dead, with no charger in sight. You can’t find the piece of paper with yesterday’s meeting notes.

None of these small issues necessitates a complete office makeover. Sometimes you just need a small upgrade to make life easier, like a charging station for your devices, a lamp that puts light where you need it or a voice recorder that transcribes meetings for you.

Black Friday is one of the best times to shop for office technology. The right purchase can remove everyday irritations — or simply make your workspace more pleasant — at a discounted price.

The selections below cover ten different uses of technology, all confirmed Black Friday bargains. The aim is a better-equipped office.

Tired of taking meeting notes? Let AI do it for you. The Pocket AI voice recorder captures every word of a meeting and offers a transcript as well as an AI summary in the app. It lasts up to four days on a single charge. The only downside is that without a premium subscription, recordings only last 30 days in the app. The subscription costs $30 per month for unlimited summaries and the highest-quality transcription. Pocket has sold more than 200,000 devices so far. A Black Friday deal brings the price of the recorder down 25% from $159 to $119.

Former Twitter engineers Abdur Chowdhury and Eric Jensen launched Aura in 2016 to help families connect through shared photos. The device has been popular every year around the holidays as a meaningful gift. Multiple people can connect to a picture frame and send images and videos to the frame via text or through the app. They can also preload photos, videos or messages to the frame before gifting. Aura doesn’t charge storage or subscription fees, so users can upload unlimited images. The 10-inch picture frame is 41% off for Black Friday, so it costs $139 instead of $234.

Everyone in an office or home environment can add their events and schedules directly on this smart calendar. They can instantly synchronize their schedules and collaborate, drawing data from sources like Google Calendar and Outlook. Users simply plug in, connect to Wi-Fi and sync their calendars within a few minutes. The calendar’s design allows it to easily fit on a table, countertop or wall, and it has a 15-inch touchscreen display. On Black Friday, the price drops from $320 to $270, a 16% reduction.

#5436. Mortgage hires: Genworth names CEO, FHLB New York elects chair

Recent mortgage industry announcements include Genworth CEO Thomas McInerney stepping down and Jerome Upton taking over; Charles Kilbourne's election as FHLB New York board chair, Darrell Boan joining Element Home Loans in Greensboro, North Carolina; and Fannie Mae appointing David Shafer to its board and approving $4.75 million in executive retention awards.  AI Summary

Thomas J. McInerney, president and CEO of Genworth Financial, has stepped down from his roles at the company and its board of directors to focus on his health, the company announced. The board appointed Jerome T. Upton, its current chief financial officer, as president, CEO and director. Upton will remain CFO through Dec. 31, with Angela Simmons expected to assume the role on Jan. 1, 2027.

Fannie Mae appointed David Shafer to its board of directors effective Nov. 23. His term will end at the next annual board election, or if he resigns or is removed by the Federal Housing Finance Agency. His committee assignments have not yet been determined.

The company also entered into retention agreements with four executives totaling $4.75 million. Chief financial officer Chryssa Halley and chief investment officer Erik Bisso will each receive $1.5 million, multifamily executive vice president Kelly Follain will receive $1 million, and chief risk officer Anthony Moon will receive $750,000.

The awards will be paid in two equal installments, in December 2026 and December 2027, provided the executives remain employed and comply with the agreements, according to filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

The Federal Home Loan Bank of New York elected Charles E. Kilbourne, managing director of the Financial Services Volunteer Corps and an independent director since 2019, as board chair for a two-year term beginning Jan. 1, 2027. Kilbourne, who chairs the board’s housing committee, will succeed Chris Martin, who is retiring at the end of this year after more than a decade of service.

Element Home Loans, a division of NFM Lending, has hired Darrell Boan as branch manager in Greensboro, North Carolina, as the company expands its presence in the Southeast. Boan, who has more than 25 years of mortgage industry experience, will lead local growth, support loan originators, and build relationships with clients and community partners.

#5435. The referral source real estate agents overlook is sitting in the next office

A durable client pipeline can come from agent referral partners. Start with colleagues in your brokerage, then expand through events, committees and cross market relationships built on follow through.  AI Summary

I’ve spent more than 25 years in this business, and one pattern has held strong in every market I’ve worked in: the agents who build lasting careers rarely do it alone. They have a network of fellow agents who think of them first when a client needs help. At The Agency, we were built on that idea. We encourage our agents to reach across the aisle, even to competitors, because when agents collaborate, more deals get done and clients are better served.

Referrals between agents get less attention than they deserve. We talk constantly about our sphere of influence, past clients and social media. Yet a colleague who’s relocating a client to your market, or who’s overbooked and can’t take on a new listing, might hand you a deal worth far more than a month of lead generation. Those opportunities only come to agents who’ve earned a place in someone’s mind.

Your brokerage is the most natural place to begin, and it’s often the most overlooked. Most of us share an office, a leadership team and a set of tools with dozens or even hundreds of agents, and many of us barely know their names.

Introduce yourself. Show up at the sales meeting, the training and the broker open, and stay for the conversation afterward. Ask people what they specialize in, what kind of client they love working with, and what they’d happily hand off. You’ll learn who’s the go-to for condos, who knows the hillside neighborhoods best, and who’s the strongest negotiator in the building.

That knowledge pays off quickly. When a client mentions a need outside your expertise, you’ll know exactly who to call. When a colleague gets a request that fits your strengths, they’ll know to call you. Trust inside a brokerage builds slowly, but once it’s there, it makes everyone’s business stronger.

Competition is part of this industry, and I won’t pretend otherwise. But the agent across the street at another firm is also a potential partner, and the best ones treat them that way.

Think about how much of real estate is geographic. Clients move across the country, across the state, sometimes across town into a different market. Your client in Los Angeles who’s buying in Aspen needs someone they can trust on the ground, and you can’t be that person. A thoughtful agent in Aspen, whom you’ve met and vetted, can. The same goes in reverse. That’s a referral built on mutual respect, and it often leads to repeat business flowing both ways for years.

Industry events, local board committees and MLS involvement are all excellent places to meet these people. You see how people handle disagreement, how they treat staff, and how they follow through. That’s the kind of insight no online profile will give you.

If you want referrals, you have to be worth referring. When one agent sends a client to another, they’re putting their own reputation on the line. They want to know that their client will be taken care of, that communication will be prompt, and that the deal will be handled with integrity.

So treat every interaction with another agent as an audition, whether or not it’s a referral situation. Return calls quickly. Show up prepared. Be the person who makes a tough negotiation easier instead of harder. Agents remember who was gracious under pressure, and they remember who wasn’t.

Close the loop, too. If someone sends you a client, keep them updated and thank them, even when the deal takes months. It sounds small, but plenty of agents forget, and the ones who don’t stand out.

I’d encourage agents to build  a simple structure around this. Set a goal to connect with a few new agents each month, one or two inside your brokerage and a few outside it. Grab coffee or hop on a quick call. Send a note when you see a colleague’s listing go under contract. Ask how you can be useful before you ask for anything.

It doesn’t take much time, just consistency and a willingness to see other agents as allies. Your next client might be working with an agent down the hall right now, or with one in a brokerage across the country. Sooner or later, that client will ask for a recommendation. Make sure the agent who gets asked already knows you.

Rainy Hake Austin is a brokerage leader at The Agency.

#5433. Who should referee a national MLS, brokers or a neutral body?

The piece supports national listing standardization but opposes a broker-controlled system. It argues the operator should be neutral, like payment networks, to protect competition and limit reliance on private channels.  AI Summary

When Open Real Estate was announced, the question of a national listing system moved back to the center of our industry. I am early in my read on this particular initiative. But I have spent a long time on the underlying question, enough that I have written a white paper of more than 70 pages on why a broker-controlled national MLS is the wrong design and what a right one would look like. For the leaders reading this, I want to lay out the core of that thinking, because this is a decision our industry may actually make in the next few years, and we should make it with our eyes open.

First, credit where it is due. A coalition of large brokerages banded together and put their names to a public position. That takes coordination and conviction, and it is plainly a response to a real and growing trend, the migration of listings into private and exclusive channels that never touch the open market. The concern is legitimate. When inventory moves into walled gardens, buyers see less, agents compete on access instead of expertise, and the consumer is quietly disadvantaged. Leaders who are worried about that are worried about the right thing.

I see two problems, one practical and one structural, and the structural one is the one that should concern every leader who does not run one of the three or four largest firms in the country.

The practical problem is straightforward. The founders have said that Open Real Estate is not a national MLS and is not meant to replace local MLSs. Whatever we call it, it is built to function as shared national listing infrastructure, and that infrastructure includes a participant view option, where a listing can be seen only by agents at participating brokerages and cannot be publicly marketed by anyone. In other words, the model does not stop private listings. It gives them a larger, better-organized home. The exact behavior this is meant to counter can continue, and we have built a bigger shared system that still has walls inside it.

Consider the architecture we have now. Hundreds of local MLSs operate across the country. We complain about that fragmentation endlessly, and it does create real friction for agents and consumers. But the fragmentation also delivers a benefit almost no one names. Each MLS acts as its own silo, its own firewall. Because the data lives in hundreds of independent repositories, no single company controls the national market. There is a series called Silo that captures the idea well. Each silo runs itself, and no one can command the whole system. Our MLS structure has handed us that same protection almost by accident. The walls are inconvenient, and the walls are also the reason no one firm owns the country’s data.

Now collapse all of it into one national system, whatever label it carries, and ask the only question that matters. Who runs it? If the answer is that brokers run it, then the brokers with the deepest pockets will control the nation’s listing infrastructure. The independents, the single-office shops, the regional firms, they will have little to no voice. Whoever sits atop a broker-controlled national system writes the rules for everyone downstream, including their direct competitors. That is not a free market with shared plumbing. That is a tollgate owned by a few, and everyone else pays to pass through.

Powerfact: Whoever controls a national MLS controls the terms of competition for every agent in the country. That cannot be a competitor.

So, let me be clear that I am not against unification. A national MLS done correctly would be a real asset. It would let an agent see listings nationwide rather than stitching together access market by market. It would mean one playbook, the same rules, forms, and fields in every state, so practicing across state lines or relocating would not require relearning the mechanics each time. That consistency would benefitagents, brokers, and consumers. The debate should not be unify or do not unify. The fight is already here, and it should be about who holds the technology in the middle.

And we already have a proven answer inside our own economy. Visa and MasterCard.

The first bank card came from Bank of America. When other banks saw it working, each began building its own card and its own processing, and the result was chaos, because every bank set different rules and the consumer experience depended on which card you carried. The resolution was not to let the largest bank operate everyone else’s cards. It was Visa, a separate entity sitting in the middle. Each bank still runs its own business and competes on its own terms. The technology and the standards that make the system uniform for the consumer are handled by a neutral party that no single bank owns.

That is the template for a national MLS. Not control by the largest brokerages, but a neutral, broker-independent organization that operates the technology and maintains uniform rules, while every brokerage, large and small, continues to run its own business and compete on skill and service. Keep each firm a silo where it should be a silo. Make the shared rails in the middle belong to no one in particular. That is the only structure that stays fair to the smallest independent and the largest franchise at the same time.

When the next national platform is announced, and there will be more of them, do not evaluate it on the feature list. Evaluate it on governance. Ask who owns it, who sits on the board, how the rules get changed, and what recourse a small brokerage has if the controlling firms decide to change the terms. If the governance concentrates power in a handful of competitors, the convenience on the surface is not worth the dependency underneath. If the governance looks like Visa, neutral, independent, and accountable to all participants rather than to the biggest ones, then we may finally have something worth building.

I appreciate the effort behind Open Real Estate, and I share the concern that prompted it. But good intentions do not fix bad architecture. A national listing system run by brokers would trade the problem of private listings for the larger problem of a privatized commons, owned by the few and rented to the many. We can do better, and we have a model sitting in our wallets that shows us how. Build the referee first. Then build the league.

Darryl Davis, CSP, is a national speaker, real estate coach, and the bestselling author of How to Become a Power Agent® in Real Estate. Learn more at darrylspeaks.com.

#5432. Wireless networking chip startup Altair nabs $100M investment

Altair Semiconductor Ltd., a supplier of wireless networking chips for connected devices, today announced that it has raised $100 million in funding.

Maverick Silicon led the Series A round. It was reportedly joined by Pitango, which invested $50 million in Altair when it spun out of Sony Corp. earlier this year. The Japanese electronics giant is said to have retained a stake.

Connected devices such as wearables and industrial sensors transmit their data traffic via the same carrier infrastructure as smartphones. However, they access that infrastructure in different ways. Connected devices using specialized, low-power network protocols to exchange data with each one and to upload readings to cloud-based backends.

Altair’s flagship modem chip, the ALT1550, supports several such protocols. The most advanced technology in the lineup is the 5G NR eRedCap protocol, which uses 5G networks to transmit data. It consumes significantly less power than a standard smartphone connection and can transmit up to 233 megabits per second.

The ALT1550 also supports two alternative protocols called LTE-M and Cat 1bis. Both use 4G network infrastructure, which is more widely available than the latest 5G hardware. LTE-M can process up to 1 megabits per second, while Cat 1bis is ten times faster and uses more power.

The chip combines a transceiver that picks up and generates radio signals with a baseband processor. That’s a chip specifically optimized for wireless networking tasks. It’s supported by an onboard memory pool, power management circuits and a module that can connect to a satellite when there’s no cell tower nearby.

The ALT1550 is one of several chips offered by Altair. An earlier module, the ALT1255, supports a network protocol called NB-IoT that uses even less power than LTE-M and Cat 1bis. It’s designed for devices that only transmit data every few weeks or months. The ALT1255 provides additional power savings by deactivating many of its features when it’s not in use.

Altair says that its silicon can be found in millions of devices. Utilities use it to power smart meters, which automatically transmit usage data to the cloud and thereby remove the need for manual readings. Delivery companies can use Altair chips to track the location of their trucks. The company’s modules also power medical devices, street lights and a wide range of other systems.

Altair will use its new funding round to kick off the mass production of its flagship ALT1550 chip. Additionally, the company plans to develop new networking products and grow its international presence.

#5429. Arrvel's New Panel PC Series: Fanless Industrial PCs Built for Harsh Edge Environments

SHENZHEN, China, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Industrial edge computing is facing a reliability crisis. As manufacturers, power utilities, and commercial operators push digitization deeper onto the factory floor and into unattended field environments, the hardware tasked with running MES terminals, SCADA front-ends, and self-service kiosks is routinely failing under conditions it was never designed to survive. Sustained vibration, metal particulate infiltration, electromagnetic interference, and wide temperature swings continue to expose the fragility of consumer-grade tablets and commercial PCs in 24/7 operational settings. Today, Arrvel is addressing that gap with the launch of its industrial panel pc seriesâa family of integrated panel pc solutions that combine industrial-grade displays, projected capacitive touchscreens, embedded processing, and extensive control interfaces inside a fanless, fully sealed aluminum chassis. Unlike standard commercial PCs, these industrial PCs are engineered specifically for continuous industrial duty.

Industrial Touch Panel PC Engineering for Continuous Operation

The Arrvel industrial touch panel pc lineup is built around a unified thermal, mechanical, and electrical architecture that prioritizes longevity over aesthetics. The chassis employs a CNC-machined front bezel paired with a one-piece extruded-aluminum rear heat sink. The anodized oxidation surface treatment increases thermal radiation efficiency, while the fin structure expands surface area by a factor of three to fiveâenough to dissipate heat from sustained CPU loads without any moving parts. Environmental hardening extends beyond thermal management. The front panel carries an IP65 ingress protection rating, sealing against dust and low-pressure water jets. The hardware platform operates across a -10 Â°C to 50 Â°C temperature range and withstands Â±8 kV air discharge and Â±4 kV contact discharge ESD events. At the same time, the units are designed to tolerate continuous vibration, equipment impact, and strong electromagnetic interferenceâconditions that typically cause touch drift, data corruption, or outright failure in standard computing hardware.

The result is a fanless industrial pc design rated for more than 50,000 hours of operational life, a critical metric for enterprises calculating total cost of ownership (TCO) across multi-year depreciation cycles. Installation flexibility is equally robust, with support for VESA arm, wall-mount, panel-embed, and desktop stand configurations, allowing the same industrial panel pc hardware to adapt from cramped machine-control enclosures to centralized dispatch consoles.

Windows Panel PC and Android Panel PC Options

Arrvel is launching the series with three distinct modelsâN15L6, A15L6, and K12L2âeach targeting different performance tiers, software ecosystems, and price points while sharing the same hardened thermal, mechanical, and electrical architecture.

The N15L6 serves as the workhorse for windows panel pc deployments in industrial automation and MES/ESOP environments. For Android-native environments and emerging edge-AI workloads, the A15L6 is Arrvel's flagship android panel pc, adopting the Rockchip RK3576 system-on-chip. Built on an 8 nm process, the RK3576 features eight cores running at up to 2.2 GHz and integrates a dedicated 6 TOPS NPU for on-device inference. Compared to the legacy RK3399, Arrvel cites a 45 percent improvement in single-threaded performance and a 130â140 percent lift in multi-threaded throughput. The unit ships with Android 14, 4 GB of RAM, and 64 GB of storage, and uniquely includes Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.4, and onboard 4G LTE connectivity as standardâreducing peripheral clutter in mobile kiosk and remote monitoring applications.

At the high-performance tier, the K12L2 stands as Arrvel's high-performance panel pc, upgrading to the Intel Core i5-1235U processor with Windows 11, again paired with 8 GB of RAM and 128 GB of storage. This configuration targets complex machine-vision gateways, multi-protocol industrial data concentrators, and graphics-intensive HMI visualization where multi-threaded processing and rapid I/O throughput are non-negotiable.

Industrial Panel Mount PC Customization and I/O Flexibility

A persistent pain point in industrial digitization is the interface mismatch between modern computing platforms and legacy field equipment. Arrvel addresses this with a densely populated, standard I/O array across the industrial panel mount pc series: dual USB 2.0 Type-A ports, dual USB 3.0 Type-A ports, one HDMI output, one VGA output, one Gigabit RJ45 Ethernet port, dual RS232 serial ports (with COM2 configurable to RS485), dedicated line-in and line-out audio jacks, and a 12 V DC input. Beyond the baseline configuration, Arrvel offers extensive factory-level customization. Processor options range from low-power Intel platforms (N5095, J1900, J6412) through 4th to 12th generation Intel Core i3, i5, and i7 processors. Memory scales from 4 GB to 64 GB, and storage options span 64 GB eMMC up to 1 TB SSD, with an optional 2.5-inch mechanical hard drive bay for data-logging-intensive applications. Operating system support covers Windows XP through Windows 11 and mainstream Linux distributions, protecting customers with legacy software dependencies.

Display sizes range from 10.1 inchesâoptimized for embedded machine-control panelsâto 21.5 inches for centralized monitoring stations, with ten intermediate sizes available. HMI Panel Applications Across Industrial Scenarios

Arrvel has architected the hmi panel series around four primary verticals where hardware failure carries disproportionate operational and financial consequences.

In manufacturing execution systems (MES) and electronic standard operating procedures (ESOP), the units replace paper-based work instructions and intermittent manual data entry. Deployed at individual workstations, the panel pc devices push real-time work orders, quality benchmarks, and digital SOPs directly to operators. Touch-based task acknowledgment and exception reporting close the manufacturing data loop without the transcription errors and multi-hour latency inherent in paper logs.

For industrial automation and CNC machine interfaces, the fanless sealed architecture prevents metal dust and cutting-fluid mist from penetrating the system, while the wide-temperature rating and EMI hardening maintain signal integrity in electrically noisy environments adjacent to variable frequency drives and high-current switching equipment. The result is a stable hmi panel that does not suffer from touchscreen drift or system lockups during critical machining cycles.

In electrical power monitoring and substation automation, the units function as localized HMI nodes connected directly to protection relays and remote terminal units via serial and Ethernet links. The wide-voltage input tolerance and EMC-compliant design mitigate data jitter and touchscreen drift caused by grid transients and strong magnetic fields, supporting true 7Ã24 monitoring reliability.

Finally, in unattended commercial self-service and smart healthcare terminals, the strengthened glass and IP65 front panel withstand abrasive cleaning, high-frequency touch interactions, and accidental liquid ingress. The absence of cooling fans eliminates a primary vector for dust accumulation and acoustic noise, supporting continuous operation with reduced preventive maintenance cyclesâcritical for kiosks and medical check-in terminals where downtime directly impacts revenue and patient throughput.

The Arrvel panel pc series represents a deliberate engineering response to the hidden costs of deploying consumer-grade computing hardware in industrial environments. By combining passive thermal management, IP65 front-panel protection, wide-voltage and wide-temperature operation, and a modular I/O philosophy across both x86 and ARM architectures, Arrvel offers system integrators and end-users an industrial panel pc platform that is configurable to the application rather than adapted through aftermarket accessories. #5428. SAP reportedly plans to lay off 10,000+ employees amid AI push

Enterprise software giant SAP SE is reportedly planning to lay off at least 10,000 employees, or more than 9% of its workforce.

Bloomberg today cited sources as saying that the scope of the restructuring initiative is still subject to change.

According to the publication, SAP and a labor council in its home country of Germany have negotiated an “employment guarantee” that will run through 2028. That may mean the layoffs will mainly affect employees in other markets. The report indicates that SAP’s product, engineering and sales units are expected to see the largest cuts.

Executives have reportedly also asked other departments to find cost reduction opportunities.

The reported restructuring push follows a banner quarter for SAP. The company’s sales and adjusted profit both topped analyst expectations. Its €24.11 billion cloud contract backlog, a measure of future revenue, also came in ahead of the consensus estimate.

The planned layoffs are said to be connected to SAP’s efforts to integrate more artificial intelligence features into its products. The company is best known for its ERP, or enterprise resource planning, software. Enterprises use it to automate a long list of backoffice tasks and share data between teams. SAP also sells cloud services for other use cases such as sales automation and customer support.

At a May user conference, the company introduced an AI interface called Joule Work for its applications. SAP says that the tool will enable workers to centrally access its products instead of navigating multiple screens.

Joule Work made its debut alongside a suite of AI agents dubbed Joule Assistants. According to SAP, they will use over 200 subagents to automate repetitive business tasks. Another new offering, Industry AI, will automate sector-specific workflows.

The report that SAP is preparing for job cuts doesn’t come as a complete surprise. Last week, Chief Financial Officer Dominik Asam told attendees of an investor event that the company expects its headcount to decline. Additionally, two of the software maker’s six directors will reportedly leave in connection with its shift to a more AI-centric strategy.

It’s unclear when the job cuts will take place. According to Bloomberg, SAP historically announced workforce reduction programs in January. The software maker took that route with its last major restructuring initiative, which saw it axe about 10,000 roles in 2024. The initiative cost about €3 billion.

The company said in a statement that “SAP continuously reviews its organization to ensure it remains aligned with its strategy and customer needs.”

ORANGE COUNTY, Calif., Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- SoCal Digital Marketing, an established SEO and digital advertising agency serving businesses throughout Southern California and nationwide, announces the launch of its new ChatGPT Ads Management Services.

The new service helps businesses explore advertising opportunities within ChatGPT through account setup, campaign strategy, ad creation, conversion tracking, and ongoing optimization.

With ChatGPT advertising continuing to expand during its beta rollout, SoCal Digital Marketing is positioning itself to help businesses evaluate this emerging channel and reach prospective customers during AI-powered research and purchasing decisions.

Bringing Real-World Advertising Experience to ChatGPT Ads

Founded in 2012, SoCal Digital Marketing has spent more than a decade helping businesses improve their online visibility, generate qualified leads, and manage paid advertising campaigns.

The agency has already helped clients establish and manage ChatGPT advertising accounts during beta access, gaining firsthand experience with the platform's evolving campaign structure, advertising relevance signals, and management capabilities.

Founder Andrew Guida has also completed ChatGPT Ads training hosted by OpenAI, building on his experience in SEO and digital advertising dating back to 2011.

"We've spent years helping businesses reach customers through Google Ads, and ChatGPT advertising represents an exciting new opportunity," said Andrew Guida, founder of SoCal Digital Marketing. "What's particularly interesting is how the platform evaluates relevance. Instead of depending primarily on the exact keywords someone searches, ChatGPT Ads considers the broader context of what someone is researching and trying to accomplish."

Guida added, "We've already been helping clients set up and manage accounts during beta access. That practical experience allows us to approach this new advertising channel with a better understanding of its capabilities, challenges, and opportunities."

A New Approach to Reaching Potential Customers

Unlike traditional Google Search advertising, which relies heavily on keyword targeting, ChatGPT Ads uses conversational context and other relevance signals to help determine when sponsored advertisements may be useful.

For example, a business owner researching manufacturing services, software solutions, or professional service providers may encounter an eligible advertisement relevant to their current research.

This creates an additional opportunity for businesses to reach prospective customers while they are comparing solutions and considering their next steps.

Why Businesses Should Consider ChatGPT Advertising Early

As a relatively new advertising platform, ChatGPT Ads may present opportunities for early adopters to begin testing campaigns before advertiser participation becomes more widespread.

While lower costs and stronger conversions are not guaranteed, businesses that begin exploring the platform can start learning which advertising messages, customer needs, and landing pages generate meaningful results.

"There's a potential advantage to learning a new advertising platform while it's still developing," Guida explained. "Businesses that begin testing ChatGPT Ads now can gather valuable information about customer behavior and campaign performance. The goal isn't simply to advertise somewhere new. It's to determine whether ChatGPT can become another reliable source of qualified leads."

SoCal Digital Marketing views ChatGPT advertising as a complement to traditional SEO, Google Ads, and Answer Engine Optimization (AEO), rather than a replacement for these established marketing strategies.

The agency's expanded services are designed to help manufacturers, franchises, professional service providers, and other eligible businesses evaluate opportunities to reach customers through AI-powered advertising.

Founded in 2012 by Andrew Guida, SoCal Digital Marketing is a California-based digital marketing agency specializing in search engine optimization (SEO), Google Ads management, Answer Engine Optimization (AEO/GEO), and lead-generation strategies.

The agency works with businesses throughout Orange County, San Diego, and the United States, including industrial manufacturers, franchises, professional service providers, and multi-location organizations.

SoCal Digital Marketing emphasizes personalized service, transparent reporting, and marketing strategies focused on measurable business results.

#5425. Hurt By Inflation? Here Are 13 Real-World Ways To Cut Costs In Your Business

You're viewing the US website. Looking for the Site edition?

With inflation still running hot, these simple moves can trim your business costs without slowing you down.

Opinions expressed by Entrepreneur contributors are their own.

Inflation remains stubborn. Producer prices are now running at a 6.5% annual clip, and affordability is top of mind. Want to cut some costs in your business? Of course you do.  Try these moves.

Both ChatGPT and Claude offer connections to your bank account and credit card services. Or, if you’re nervous about that, just upload your statements.  You’ll be impressed by the number of suggestions they make to reduce your spending and better manage expenses.

I used to think canceling online subscriptions would be a big headache, and years ago it was. Not anymore. Search for “cancel my subscription on Google Play” (or Apple or Amazon), and you’ll get direct links to do it. I’m betting you and your business have subscriptions you’ve forgotten about that are eating up hundreds of dollars a year.

Every year, put your business and auto insurance policies out for a quote. Ask your AI chatbot to make suggestions too. This is not very time-consuming and can be accomplished using an administrative person in your office. We’re oftentimes too lazy to do this.  And that’s costing us.

Many of my clients have complicated, expensive coffee machines in their break rooms with a wide variety of coffees. They also stock sugar packets, teas, mini creamers, plastic stirrers and paper cups. It’s too much. Offer fewer coffees so you order less. Put out a sugar bowl, bring in a gallon of creamer and go back to ceramic mugs. Call me Scrooge, but it saves money.

NerdWallet does a great job regularly reviewing business and personal credit cards. Again, use your AI chatbot to look at your spending and tell it your preferences and you’ll get plenty of recommendations too.  Moving to a better card could earn you more points and cashback rewards then you’re getting right now. I have some clients that regularly switch back and forth.

Speaking of credit, if your business buys products on Amazon, then make sure you use one of Amazon’s credit cards for purchases.  With a Prime membership, you can earn 5% back on eligible Amazon purchases, and there’s no annual fee.

If you can’t pay off a credit card purchase right away from operations, consider using working capital or a lower-rate loan to reduce the balance. Credit card interest rates are high, so this can cut what you pay in interest significantly.

This is a very common tax move, yet so many of us ignore it. Put as much as you can into your retirement plan to lower your tax bill this year.  When you save – assuming you’re eligible – sock money into a Roth IRA or Roth 401K so your after-tax money grows tax-free.  With a Roth, there are no minimum distributions, and you can take the money out whenever you want, provided it meets certain requirements like a first-time home purchase, higher education or unreimbursed medical expenses.

Make sure your company has an HSA and contribute the max. It will reduce your tax expense and allow you to save money for future healthcare expenses.

Every square foot your inventory takes up costs you in overhead and space. Twice a year, take a hard look at your inventory and get rid of what isn’t moving. Sell it on Craigslist, eBay or Facebook Marketplace or scrap it.

Mark Cuban’s Cost Plus Drugs and Amazon Pharmacy both offer options that let businesses provide discounted prescription drugs, and they work with many popular health plans.

Set up a donor-advised fund and contribute to it this year, even if you haven’t decided which charities or nonprofits will receive the money. You take the deduction now and choose the recipients later.

I like Capital One Shopping. Add it as a browser extension for yourself and anyone else who makes purchases for your business. Whenever someone is on a shopping site, it searches for available coupons before you buy. It works about half the time, and it has saved me significant money over the years.

We can all afford the things we want — it’s just that sometimes we choose to spend our money on other things instead. That’s fine. But know that cutting back on things like travel, entertainment, subscriptions, marketing or other discretionary spending in your business (and your personal life) can help you reallocate your cash for other purposes.  You’re more in control than you think.

Inflation remains stubborn. Producer prices are now running at a 6.5% annual clip, and affordability is top of mind. Want to cut some costs in your business? Of course you do.  Try these moves.

Both ChatGPT and Claude offer connections to your bank account and credit card services. Or, if you’re nervous about that, just upload your statements.  You’ll be impressed by the number of suggestions they make to reduce your spending and better manage expenses.

I used to think canceling online subscriptions would be a big headache, and years ago it was. Not anymore. Search for “cancel my subscription on Google Play” (or Apple or Amazon), and you’ll get direct links to do it. I’m betting you and your business have subscriptions you’ve forgotten about that are eating up hundreds of dollars a year.

#5424. Ruko Launches F11PRO 2 Plus (RC4), Bringing an Upgraded Aerial Photography Experience with a 5.5-Inch Touchscreen Controller

HONG KONG, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Ruko is excited to announce the launch of its latest drone, the F11PRO 2 Plus (RC4), now available on Amazon. Designed to deliver an upgraded aerial photography experience, the new drone features an integrated 5.5-inch touchscreen remote controller, advanced 8K imaging, enhanced flight stabilization, and intelligent flight capabilities. Combining intuitive controls with stable flight performance and creative aerial features, it makes capturing memorable moments from above easier and more enjoyable.

Enhanced Imaging for More Detailed Aerial Photography

Whether you're capturing a family vacation, exploring scenic landscapes, or documenting outdoor adventures, the Ruko F11PRO 2 Plus (RC4) helps turn everyday experiences into memorable aerial footage. Its advanced camera system supports high-resolution 8K (7680 Ã 4320) photography and 4K/30fps video recording, capturing rich details and vibrant scenes from above. The AI-enhanced Night Mode further improves image brightness and detail in low-light conditions, making it easier to capture the beauty of evening landscapes, sunset views, and nighttime gatherings.

An Upgraded Touchscreen Remote for Greater Convenience

A standout addition is the RC4 touchscreen remote controller, which offers a more direct and convenient way to enjoy aerial photography. Its built-in 5.5-inch 1080P HD display provides a clear view of live footage, while its 1200-nit high brightness helps users see the screen even under strong sunlight. With automatic connection upon startup and support for simultaneous viewing on a smartphone, the controller simplifies setup and makes the entire flying experience more intuitive.

Advanced Flight Stabilization for Greater Control and Confidence

The F11PRO 2 Plus (RC4) incorporates multiple positioning technologies, including VIO, TOF, GPS, and a barometer, to support stable hovering and more precise flight control. These technologies work together to help the drone maintain its position and navigate more steadily in suitable environments. Intelligent safety features, including landing pad recognition, multiple Return-to-Home options, and a built-in buzzer for locating the drone, provide additional reassurance throughout the flight, helping even beginners enjoy a more confident flying experience.

To further enhance image quality during flight, the F11PRO 2 Plus (RC4) features a 3-axis brushless gimbal that helps maintain stable, smooth footage. By combining mechanical stabilization with its high-quality imaging system, the drone helps reduce unwanted camera movement, allowing users to capture clearer aerial videos and more refined photos across a variety of outdoor settings.

Intelligent Tracking and Automated Flight for Creative Shots

For those looking to create more dynamic content, the F11PRO 2 Plus (RC4) offers intelligent subject tracking and automated camera movements. Users can choose from different tracking modes to follow moving subjects, while one-touch cinematic flight options make it easier to capture creative shots without complicated manual operation. Combined with GPS-assisted flight modes such as orbit flight and waypoint planning, these features open up more possibilities for capturing travel memories, outdoor adventures, and engaging social media content.

10KM Digital Transmission for Expansive Aerial Exploration

#5423. XRP News: Thanksgiving Rally or December 1 Supply Shock?

The CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

XRP has a history of making Thanksgiving interesting, old news for some. In 2024, Ripple surged nearly 49% in the three days following the holiday. Last year, it went nowhere. Now, XRP is heading into another Thanksgiving with $1 in sight and Ripple’s 1 billion-token escrow unlock looming on December 1.

The timing puts bulls in a tight spot. XRP is recovering from a November sell-off, but the rebound has yet to clear major resistance. A holiday rally could give buyers some breathing room before next week’s token release puts supply back in the spotlight.

The 2024 Thanksgiving weekend was anything but quiet for XRP. The token closed November 28 at $1.54, climbed to $1.80 the following day, and reached $2.29 by December 1. That was a gain of nearly 49% from Thanksgiving’s close.

The rally had fuel beyond holiday trading as Donald Trump’s election victory revived hopes for a friendlier crypto regulatory environment, while XRP was breaking out after years of being held back by its SEC lawsuit. Buyers were chasing momentum, and the long weekend did little to slow them down.

Last year’s price action was considerably less exciting. XRP closed Thanksgiving on November 27, 2025, near $2.20, then drifted around $2.16 over the following days. The market offered no repeat of the explosive move seen a year earlier.

That history makes this year’s comparison interesting, but the conditions are different. XRP is entering Thanksgiving after a painful November decline.

Discover: The Crypto Presales This Q4 2026

XRP’s recovery toward $0.95 has brought the psychological $1 level back into play. Buyers have been defending the area below $0.90, preventing another immediate breakdown and giving the short-term chart some breathing room.

But the problem is overhead resistance, as XRP must first push through $0.96–$0.98 before $1 becomes a realistic breakout target. That zone has become the immediate test for buyers. A clean move through it could attract momentum traders and open the path toward $1.02 and $1.08.

The $1 mark matters because XRP has spent November losing ground. Reclaiming it would put the token back above an important psychological threshold and give bulls something concrete to work with.

Failure to break resistance could leave the rebound looking like another dead-cat bounce. XRP’s recent low around $0.89 remains the level to watch. Losing it would put $0.86 back on the radar and risk undoing the recovery.

For now, the chart is caught between an improving short-term bounce and a damaged larger trend. Bulls have a chance, but they need to turn that chance into a breakout.

The next complication arrives Monday, with Ripple’s scheduled escrow contracts. It will release 1 billion XRP, renewing concerns about supply just as the token tries to recover from bad geopolitical news.

The billion-token headline sounds worse than Ripple’s typical net release. Over the past year, the company has re-escrowed around 70% of monthly unlocks, leaving around 300 million XRP outside escrow on average. The market will be watching whether December follows the same pattern.

The full 1 billion XRP unlock is not equivalent to 1 billion tokens hitting exchanges for sale. What Ripple re-locks, retains, or moves afterward will determine how much circulating supply actually changes.

What does it need? XRP cannot afford to enter Monday with a failed breakout and weakening support. If buyers reclaim $1 before the unlock, sentiment could shift in their favor. If XRP remains pinned below resistance, the escrow event gives nervous traders another reason to stay cautious.

Thanksgiving delivered XRP a spectacular rally in 2024. This year, bulls need more than a holiday repeat; they need the $1 back.

#5422. Zeno Power makes progress on an underwater power system that will eventually go nuclear

by Alan Boyle on Nov 19, 2026 at 7:00 amNovember 19, 2026 at 8:01 am

Zeno Power has hit a major milestone in its push to build nuclear batteries for underwater use.

The startup said today that it successfully demonstrated an electrically heated Stirling generator in a controlled maritime setting in Washington state. The two-week demonstration produced electrical power outputs in excess of 20 watts, said Lindsey Boles, Zeno’s chief product officer.

“It’s a really big step for us — just solidifying our expertise in how to design these, and then confirming our ability to translate that into operational hardware that meets or exceeds what our customers need,” Boles told GeekWire.

Zeno is developing the power system with support from the Department of Defense as a follow-up to an initial $7.5 million contract awarded in 2023. The generator uses a Stirling engine to convert heat into electricity by cycling gas through heating and cooling phases in a closed cylinder.

For the recent demonstration, the prototype device relied on an electric heating element. Future devices will instead rely on heat generated by the radioactive decay of strontium-90, a radioisotope that can be extracted from spent nuclear fuel.

Nuclear batteries have been in use for decades, primarily for space missions ranging from the Apollo moon shots to NASA’s Voyager spacecraft and Mars rovers. But the batteries being developed by Zeno Power promise to be at least four times more efficient than traditional radioisotope thermoelectric generators, Boles said.

Boles said the non-radiological test exceeded expectations. “There’s a difference between a design that works on paper and hardware that works in the field,” she said in a news release. “This is the moment our team has been building toward: proof that this technology works outside the lab.”

Long-lasting nuclear batteries could be used to power undersea sensor networks or recharge autonomous underwater vehicles. “There are a lot of applications, especially on the maritime front, that we really want electricity for,” Boles said. “And we really don’t need a ton of it. But we need it to be really reliable, and we need it to be long endurance, and we need it to be self-managed. … I think of it like a slow Tesla supercharger on the seabed.”

Retired Navy Adm. John Richardson, former chief of naval operations and a member of Zeno’s board of directors, called the recent test an “important step toward undersea superiority.”

“Protecting maritime infrastructure and powering distributed systems at sea requires energy; energy that lasts for years, not days or months,” Richardson said in a written statement. “As competition intensifies in contested domains, powered subsea systems will help keep us ahead. Zeno Power has steadily reduced risk, proven its technology, built a supply chain, and prepared to scale production.”

Next year, Zeno Power plans to install a radioisotope heat source in its generator and test the system in a water tank under controlled laboratory conditions. If those tests are successful, Zeno will move forward with the first operational seabed deployment of its radioisotope-fueled maritime system later in 2027.

The maritime battery isn’t Zeno’s only product. The company is also working on a nuclear-powered heater system for spacecraft, with a demonstration on the lunar surface planned as early as 2028. Zeno’s broader vision is to provide long-lasting, reliable power on the moon and Mars, and in extreme environments on Earth.

Since its founding in 2018, Zeno has secured $105 million in private capital and has brought in $60 million in contracts with the Pentagon and NASA. The company has more than 95 employees at locations in Seattle, California and Washington, D.C., with the largest contingent working at its engineering headquarters in Seattle’s South Lake Union district.
